_comment: Hand-curated registry of state, regional and utility programs that pay a rebate, credit or discount on the purchase or lease of a new or used EV or PHEV. Never regenerate from a scrape. One entry per program; every figure is the program's own, with the page it was read from and the date. Purchaser-side conditions are CONDITIONS TO STATE and are never evaluated by the site. Research record: docs/incentives/INCENTIVES-2026-09-02.md (gitignored, local). Consumed by web/lib/incentives/registry.ts; shape documented there.

programs.name: Connecticut CHEAPR
programs.statusNote: No funding pause stated; program page content is dated 2025-10-01, so its silence carries little weight. DEEP's own CHEAPR statistics page says the monthly data "do not reflect current available funding amounts", so no public funding-remaining figure exists. Funding is the recurring statutory account under C.G.S. 22a-202 rather than a one-off appropriation, and rebates are point-of-sale through enrolled dealers. If this ever needs settling, the CHEAPR Board's materials are the place, not the program page.

programs.name: PNM income-qualified EV purchase rebate

jurisdiction.utility: PNM (Public Service Company of New Mexico)

programs.statusNote: Owner, 2026-09-05: kept LIVE and named on New Mexico cars — "I'm not confident that program is dead and it's worth buyers checking directly, which motivated ones will." The finding that had set it to depleted stays here for the re-check: Fund essentially spent. PNM's 2025 Annual Progress Report (NMPRC docket 23-00195-UT, filed 2026-06-01) reports the Electric Vehicle Point-of-Sale (LI only) measure at 243 rebates and $972,000 paid against an $18,000 remaining balance at 2025-12-31 - already over its $900,000 design budget, topped up from the Income-Qualified Reserve for what PNM calls "this incredibly popular measure". At up to $4,000 each that is four or five rebates left, as of a report nine months old. PNM still advertises the rebate on pnmdriveelectric.com and ev.pnm.com, which is why this is "depleted" rather than paused or ended. PNM CONFIRMED the exhaustion itself on 2026-08-06: its Motion to Reopen Docket 23-00195-UT for budget flexibility (docket 26-0000155, DOC-000414653-26) lists Low-Income EV Purchase Rebates among programs that "have reached or are anticipated to reach budget exhaustion", and asks to move $840,000 into the measure ($152,500 from Residential L2 Purchase, $87,500 from Fleet L2 Make-Ready, $600,000 from Mass Transit Make-Ready) under Rule 17.9.574.14(A). As of 2026-09-05 that docket holds the motion and NO order. The identical 2025 request (filed 2025-07-10) was granted 2025-09-18, 70 days later. RE-CHECK: an order on docket 26-0000155 or 23-00195-UT - if granted, the measure is re-funded by roughly 210 rebates and goes back to live. The 2024-2026 TEP ends 2026-12-31 and PNM applied on 2026-06-01 for a 2027-2029 TEP (docket 26-0000115) carrying the measure forward.
